title: Given a Scenario, Use Common Safety Procedures

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: A technician must protect the technician, the equipment, and the environment at the same time. Match each hazard to the safety procedure that controls it.
sections.callout: Protect yourself → remove power → control static → handle equipment correctly → keep the area safe.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Recognize whether a procedure protects people from electrical or physical hazards, protects components from static and mishandling, or keeps the surrounding workplace safe.

sections.title: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD)
paragraphs: Electrostatic discharge is a sudden transfer of static electricity. A discharge too small for a person to notice can damage RAM, motherboards, processors, expansion cards, and other sensitive electronics.
sections.callout: You may not feel it; the component may still be damaged.

sections.title: ESD Straps and ESD Mats

entries.title: Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) Straps
paragraphs: An ESD wrist strap equalizes electrical potential between the technician and properly grounded equipment, preventing the technician's static charge from passing through a component.

entries.title: ESD Mats
paragraphs: An ESD mat creates a static-controlled work surface that safely dissipates charge when used correctly.

sections.callout: Person → strap; work surface → mat. They may be used together.

sections.title: Electrical Safety
paragraphs: Computers and peripherals use electricity that can shock technicians, damage equipment, or cause fire. Follow approved electrical procedures and never defeat a safety feature.

entries.title: Equipment Grounding
paragraphs: Proper equipment grounding provides a safe path for fault current and helps protect users, technicians, and equipment. Never remove a grounding prong.

sections.title: Grounding vs. ESD Protection
paragraphs: Electrical grounding protects people and equipment from dangerous electrical faults. ESD controls protect sensitive electronics from static discharge.
sections.callout: High-energy electrical fault → grounding; static charge → ESD protection.

sections.title: Proper Component Handling and Storage
paragraphs: Handle circuit boards by their edges, avoid contacts and chips, keep liquids away, and never force connectors or components. Store sensitive parts where they are protected from static, moisture, heat, impact, and disorganization.

sections.title: Cable Management
paragraphs: Good cable management improves safety, airflow, organization, troubleshooting, and access. Poor routing creates trip hazards, obstructs cooling, strains connectors, and causes accidental disconnections.
sections.callout: Inside the chassis → airflow; outside the chassis → people and trip safety.

sections.title: Antistatic Bags
paragraphs: Antistatic bags protect ESD-sensitive RAM, expansion cards, motherboards, and storage electronics during transport or storage. Ordinary plastic can generate static and is not an appropriate substitute.
sections.callout: Sensitive component not installed → antistatic bag.

sections.title: Compliance with Government Regulations
paragraphs: Technicians must follow applicable laws and regulations for workplace safety, hazardous materials, electronic waste, environmental practices, and disposal procedures.
sections.callout: Local preference may be optional; a legal requirement is not.

sections.title: Personal Safety
paragraphs: Personal safety procedures include removing electrical hazards, using correct lifting techniques, following fire procedures, and wearing eye or respiratory protection suited to the actual hazard.

sections.title: Disconnect Power Before Repairing a PC
paragraphs: Before opening or repairing a computer, shut it down and disconnect external power when appropriate. This reduces the risk of shock, short circuits, accidental startup, and component damage. Pressing the power button does not guarantee all energy is removed.
sections.callout: Protect the technician from electricity → disconnect power; protect components from technician static → ESD control.

sections.title: Lifting Techniques
paragraphs: Assess weight first, get help when needed, keep the load close, bend at the knees, lift with the legs, and avoid twisting while carrying.
sections.callout: Heavy server, UPS, or printer → use proper technique and get assistance.

sections.title: Fire Safety
paragraphs: Know emergency procedures, keep exits accessible, avoid overloaded circuits, use extinguishing equipment appropriate to the fire type, and evacuate when required. Never use an inappropriate method on energized electrical equipment.
sections.callout: Personal safety comes before saving the computer.

sections.title: Safety Goggles and Air Filter Masks

entries.title: Safety Goggles
paragraphs: Protect the eyes during work that can produce flying debris, dust, or small fragments, including authorized physical media destruction.

entries.title: Air Filter Mask
paragraphs: Helps reduce inhalation of dust and airborne particles during equipment cleaning or work in contaminated areas. Match the protection to the workplace hazard.

sections.callout: Flying material → goggles; inhalation hazard → air filter mask.

sections.title: Technician Safety Sequence
bullets: Check that the environment is safe and clear
Shut down and disconnect appropriate power
Apply ESD protection
Handle and store components correctly
Manage cables to prevent trips and blocked airflow
Use suitable personal protective equipment
Follow government and workplace requirements

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Static-safe technician → ESD strap
Static-safe bench → ESD mat
Fault-current protection → equipment grounding
RAM or circuit board → handle by the edges
Loose or obstructive wiring → cable management
Store RAM or motherboard → antistatic bag
Required safety or environmental rule → government regulation
Open computer chassis → disconnect power
Heavy server or printer → proper lifting techniques
Electrical fire → approved fire safety procedure
Flying fragments → safety goggles
Dust or airborne particles → air filter mask

sections.title: Objective 4.4 Exam Trap
bullets: ESD threatens electronic components; electrical shock threatens the technician.
An ESD strap controls charge on the technician; an ESD mat controls the work surface.
Equipment grounding protects against electrical faults; an ESD strap controls static charge.
A powered-off PC may still be connected to electrical energy; disconnect power before internal repair as appropriate.
Use an antistatic bag rather than ordinary plastic for sensitive electronics.
Goggles protect eyes from flying debris; a mask protects against inhaled particles.
Cable management is a safety and cooling requirement, not merely cosmetic.
